verses.text: When Jabin king of Hazor heard of it, he sent to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, to the king of Achshaph,
and to the kings who were on the north, in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the lowland, and in the heights of Dor on the west,
to the Canaanite on the east and on the west, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite in the hill country, and the Hivite under Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
They went out, they and all their armies with them, many people, even as the sand that is on the seashore in multitude, with very many horses and chariots.
All these kings met together; and they came and encamped together at the waters of Merom, to fight with Israel.

Yahweh said to Joshua, “Don’t be afraid because of them; for tomorrow at this time, I will deliver them up all slain before Israel. You shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”
So Joshua came suddenly, with all the warriors, against them by the waters of Merom, and attacked them.

Yahweh delivered them into the hand of Israel, and they struck them, and chased them to great Sidon, and to Misrephoth Maim, and to the valley of Mizpah eastward. They struck them until they left them no one remaining.
Joshua did to them as Yahweh told him. He hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
Joshua turned back at that time, and took Hazor, and struck its king with the sword: for Hazor used to be the head of all those kingdoms.
They struck all the souls who were in it with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying them. There was no one left who breathed. He burned Hazor with fire.
Joshua captured all the cities of those kings, with their kings, and he struck them with the edge of the sword, and utterly destroyed them; as Moses the servant of Yahweh commanded.
But as for the cities that stood on their mounds, Israel burned none of them, except Hazor only. Joshua burned that.

The children of Israel took all the plunder of these cities, with the livestock, as plunder for themselves; but every man they struck with the edge of the sword, until they had destroyed them. They didn’t leave any who breathed.
As Yahweh commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua. Joshua did so. He left nothing undone of all that Yahweh commanded Moses.
So Joshua captured all that land, the hill country, all the South, all the land of Goshen, the lowland, the Arabah, the hill country of Israel, and the lowland of the same;
from Mount Halak, that goes up to Seir, even to Baal Gad in the valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon. He took all their kings, struck them, and put them to death.
Joshua made war a long time with all those kings.
There was not a city that made peace with the children of Israel, except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon. They took all in battle.

For it was of Yahweh to harden their hearts, to come against Israel in battle, that he might utterly destroy them, that they might have no favor, but that he might destroy them, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

Joshua came at that time, and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah, and from all the hill country of Israel: Joshua utterly destroyed them with their cities.
There were none of the Anakim left in the land of the children of Israel. Only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod, did some remain.
So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that Yahweh spoke to Moses; and Joshua gave it for an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. The land had rest from war.

footnotes.content: When word reached Jabin, a king saw threat where God saw settled purpose. How many times do we gather our defenses against what the Lord has already decided? Fear is a fast messenger.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From north to south—hill country to lowland, the kings came from every quarter. United only in resistance to God's will, they would fall as one. Our alliances matter far less than whom we oppose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Anakim, the Hivites, the nations whose names had shadowed Israel's fear—they gathered, thinking number would hold back God's people. But numbers never have and never will stand against His purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Like sand on the seashore, like stars unnumbered—this ancient phrase echoes an older promise to Abraham. The enemies' vast host only underscores how faithfulness, not might, determines the outcome.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All these kings met together at the waters of Merom, their courage rising as they assembled. One might almost admire their resolve—if it were not set against the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Don't be afraid." Joshua hears the voice that has steadied his heart since Gilgal. Tomorrow's victory is already secure in the mind of God. We are invited to trust, not to wonder.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua came suddenly—not with hesitation or delay, but with the warriors ready, moving in full obedience. Faith that waits for tomorrow's promise acts decisively in today's command.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh delivered them—and Joshua's hand merely carried out what the Lord had spoken. Chase them to Sidon, to Mizpah, until none remained. God does not leave His work unfinished.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hamstring the horses, burn the chariots—Joshua moves without hesitation to do exactly as Yahweh commanded. Obedience doesn't debate; it acts. The wisdom that removes the enemy's advantage is wisdom at its truest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hazor, that great city, had been the head of kingdoms. But a city that stood against Israel now falls before Joshua's sword. Even what was mightiest is nothing before the Lord who fights for His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every soul, every breath—completely and entirely. This is conquest as covenant fulfillment, not as cruelty for its own sake. The land must be cleansed of those who would turn hearts from the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As Moses the servant commanded, so Joshua does. There is a line running from the wilderness to this moment—one purpose, one faith, faithfulness across generations. Joshua isn't changing course; he's fulfilling it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The other cities stood on their mounds—left standing, except Hazor. The Lord is particular about which strongholds fall entirely. There is wisdom in this selectivity that we may not always see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The plunder is taken—livestock, goods—but the peoples who would turn Israel away from God are utterly destroyed. Victory means more than treasure; it means the land cleansed for holiness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As Yahweh commanded Moses, Moses commanded Joshua, and Joshua did so. One Word, one servant, one obedience. There is a beauty in this chain—each link holds because each one stayed faithful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From the hill country to the Arabah, from Goshen to the lowland—the geography of promise is now the geography of possession. The land itself becomes the testimony that what God spoke has come to pass.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From Mount Halak to Baal Gad, from Seir to Lebanon—the whole breadth of the land is swept clean, every king struck down. Completeness is the mark of God's work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua made war a long time—this wasn't a quick triumph but a sustained faithfulness. Long obedience in the same direction, day after day, until the work is done.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No city made peace save Gibeon—those who chose to deceive were spared, while those who trusted their strength fell. The Lord sees the heart and honors even crooked wisdom that reaches toward Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh hardened their hearts to come against Israel. This is not cruelty but the righteous work of bringing judgment. Those who will not bend toward God cannot help but march toward their own undoing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Anakim, those giants whose very name had sent fear through Israel since the wilderness days—Joshua cut them down utterly from the hill country. The fear we have carried can be ended by a courage rooted in faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: None remained save in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod—a few refuges on the edges. The land is clean; the people are free to walk as the Lord's own, unmolested by the old terrors.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The whole land, taken as Yahweh spoke to Moses. Given to Israel by their tribes. And the land had rest from war. This is the end we were promised—not wealth or might, but peace and a home where we can serve the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
